title: Noor and the Parish
premise: Ansel Almeida, concierge at the decaying Parish Hotel on a tidal Cornish coast, receives two letters in the same week: one confessing to a drowning thirty years ago, the other promising a larger inheritance if he keeps silent. As he investigates, Ansel discovers the letters were written by his own late mother, who worked at the hotel the summer a guest's daughter vanished, and that the hotel's owner has been paying hush money ever since. The climax comes when an equinox tide exposes the old boathouse foundations and the truth: the girl drowned accidentally during a game gone wrong, and the cover-up, not the death, destroyed three families. Ansel chooses exposure over inheritance, closing the case by finally making himself visible.
about_author: Ada Kavanagh is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent a decade listening to other people's secrets through a lobby desk. They write mysteries about the invisible people who keep institutions running.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Ansel Almeida, POV. Sorting the morning post at the Parish Hotel, Ansel finds two letters addressed to him personally: one confessing to a thirty-year-old drowning, one offering money for silence. Both written in the same handwriting. The emotional beat is unease—the man who notices everything realizes someone has been noticing him.

chapters.title: The Register of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. He searches the hotel's archived guest registers from the summer of 1994 and finds his mother's name among the seasonal staff—erased from every family story he was told. The beat is vertigo: his origin story cracks open as he learns she worked here the summer Elodie Vane drowned.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and elderly Margaret Vane, POV. Ansel visits the drowned girl's mother under a pretext; Margaret recalls a perfect daughter and a suspicious staff member. Her certainty contradicts the confession letter. The beat is dramatic irony—the reader sees grief has curated her memory into something unrecognizable.

chapters.title: The Owner's Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. He discovers the hotel owner, Cyril Parish, has paid annual sums to three former employees for decades—a hush ledger hidden in plain sight as 'maintenance costs.' The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: Ansel realizes the letters are a lever being pulled on all of them.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel and retired boatman Tam Oddie, POV. Tam, one of the paid three, half-confesses over whisky: there was more than one child on the rocks that night, and the tide took something they never reported. The beat is complicity—Ansel feels the pull of silence, the same corruption that bought Tam.

chapters.title: A Second Confession
chapters.summary: Cyril Parish, POV. Confronted, Cyril admits he orchestrated the cover-up but insists the confession letter isn't his doing—and reveals the handwriting belongs to a woman long dead. The beat is reversal: the puppeteer claims to be another marionette, and Ansel must decide whether power ever truly relinquishes its grip.

chapters.title: The Mother's Box
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Following his mother's instructions left with a solicitor, Ansel opens a box containing her diary: she saw the children playing on the groyne that night and stayed silent out of fear, then spent her life drafting confessions she never sent. The beat is grief transmuted into purpose—he will finish what she couldn't.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV chapters braided together. Ansel reconstructs the night from diaries, ledgers, and tide tables, finding the alibis of Cyril, Tam, and Margaret Vane interlock too perfectly—deliberately built to protect a fourth person. The beat is intellectual triumph shadowed by horror at how thoroughly memory was engineered.

chapters.title: The Equinox Boathouse
chapters.summary: Ansel, Tam, and Margaret, POV. At the lowest equinox tide, the exposed boathouse foundations yield Elodie's locket and a child's shoe—evidence the game involved four children, including young Cyril's son, now the hotel's heir. The beat is confrontation: past and present collide as the heir arrives demanding the evidence be buried.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Refusing the heir's final offer of the inheritance, Ansel gives the evidence to Margaret Vane and the police, then pins both letters to the lobby board where guests can read them. The beat is quiet catharsis—the invisible man steps into the light, and the Parish Hotel's tide finally gives up what it took.
